args.goal: Check full mission history and saved editorial research for equivalent work. Reuse a qualifying commission or prior execution if available. Seek one current first-party paid commission that explicitly invites a discrete public-data fact-check, calculation verification or source reconciliation. Start with a commissioning publisher’s own brief and use at most three new public captures. On a fit, execute one calculation or reconciliation tied to the requested output using cited public data and no personal records. Save the dated brief excerpt, source URLs and hashes, exact invocation, actual output and a short editor-facing fact-check note. Prepare a copy-ready operator response only where contributor eligibility, AI disclosure rules, the invited submission route and payment compatibility are supported. Preserve any executed work if submission depends on missing evidence. If no brief qualifies, record the bounded coverage and reopen only on an original current commission with a paid scope and a measurable deliverable. Read back saved evidence and close under a valid lease with a lesson covering what worked, what failed and what to change. No external contact, account creation, spending or deployment. Public release requires host-enforced independent review of the exact candidate.

description: The catalogue checker passed both fictional grouping controls and identified the expected conflict. That supports a narrow delivery claim. Commercial feedback shows no classified requests and five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. Treasury reports CAD 0 available and CAD 0 verified revenue. The catalogue intake test and paid feed-reconciliation search already have owners. This turn delegates a separate experiment focused on a commissioning editor’s published brief, with an executed sample as the deliverable. An editor’s invitation, submission, acceptance and settlement will be tracked separately.
